2609.20001.title: E-AVI: Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Assessment for Automated Video Interviews
2609.20001.paper_summary: Automated video interview assessment integrates verbal content, acoustic delivery, and visual behavior, yet numerical predictions alone provide limited inspectable support. We present E-AVI, an evidence-grounded framework that extracts timestamped multimodal evidence and integrates dimension-conditioned evidence attention with source-level embeddings for scoring. A shared evidence pool further supports natural-language feedback and follow-up question answering. On RecruitView and a private hospitality dataset, E-AVI consistently outperforms fine-tuned multimodal baselines in rank correlation. Ablation, evidence-deletion, bootstrap, human-audit, and QA analyses characterize the predictive contribution, grounding, and practical utility of the evidence pathway. Together, these results demonstrate that our proposed E-AVI framework improves predictive performance while providing inspectable support for assessment, feedback, and interactive analysis.
2609.20001.paper_summary_zh: 自動化視頻面試評估整合了口頭內容、聲音表達和視覺行為，但僅僅依賴數值預測提供的可檢查支持有限。<lb/>我們提出了E-AVI，一個基於證據的框架，提取帶有時間戳的多模態證據，並將維度條件證據注意力與源級嵌入整合以進行評分。<lb/>共享證據池進一步支持自然語言反饋和後續問題回答。<lb/>在RecruitView和一個私有的酒店數據集上，E-AVI在排名相關性方面始終優於微調的多模態基準。<lb/>消融、證據刪除、自助法、人類審核和質量保證分析描述了預測貢獻、基礎和證據路徑的實用性。<lb/>綜合這些結果顯示，我們提出的E-AVI框架在提高預測性能的同時，還為評估、反饋和互動分析提供了可檢查的支持。
